title: The Order of the Scans
transcript: At a research library, requests for digital copies used to be handled in the order they arrived. Staff noticed that a request for a single letter could sit for weeks behind a request for several boxes of documents. They set aside part of each morning for small jobs so these requests could move steadily through the queue. Fragile items still went to a conservator first, since opening a tightly bound volume on a scanner could damage it. The library also began telling readers when their requests were likely to be ready. This reduced follow-up messages, even though the staff were scanning about the same number of pages.

questions.prompt: What drawback did the original queue have?
options: A large request could hold up a much smaller one.
Requests for letters often arrived without enough information.
Staff routinely processed the same documents twice.
Requests from frequent readers were automatically moved ahead.
questions.answer: A large request could hold up a much smaller one.
questions.explanation: 按收到的先后顺序处理，扫描一封信的请求可能排在几箱文件之后，等上好几周。

questions.prompt: What effect did giving readers estimated completion times have?
options: It increased the number of pages scanned each week.
It led readers to request smaller batches of documents.
It reduced the number of messages asking about requests.
It made readers more likely to collect physical documents.
questions.answer: It reduced the number of messages asking about requests.
questions.explanation: 告知预计完成时间后，读者追问进度的消息少了。
